item.title: Fiji to face France, Croatia and Egypt at Handball Youth World Championship this week
item.description: 12 young Fijian women are preparing to carry the nation’s hopes on the international stage as they compete at the International Handball Federation (IHF) Women’s Youth World Championship in Romania. The Fiji Under-18 girls’ handball team will make history when they take part in the global tournament, facing some of the world’s top young handball nations in the group stage.
item.content:encoded:
12 young Fijian women are preparing to carry the nation’s hopes on the international stage as they compete at the International Handball Federation (IHF) Women’s Youth World Championship in Romania.

The Fiji Under-18 girls’ handball team will make history when they take part in the global tournament, facing some of the world’s top young handball nations in the group stage.

Fiji will begin its campaign against France on Wednesday, July 29, before facing Croatia on Thursday, July 30. The team will then complete its group-stage matches against Egypt on Saturday, August 1.

The young athletes have been working hard in preparation for the challenge and are determined to represent Fiji with pride against established handball nations.

Their journey to Romania has received a significant boost through support from the Office of the Prime Minister and the Chinese Embassy in Fiji, with funding assistance helping the team meet preparation and participation costs.

The support has been welcomed as a major contribution towards ensuring the players and officials can take part in Fiji’s first appearance at the prestigious international competition.

item.title: Suva Funeral Directors denies overcrowding claims
item.description: The Ministry of Health says it will continue discussions with the privately operated Suva Funeral Directors over concerns about morgue overcrowding. However, the company has strongly denied there has ever been a shortage of storage space or that families have been turned away.
item.content:encoded:
The Ministry of Health says it will continue discussions with the privately operated Suva Funeral Directors over concerns about morgue overcrowding.

However, the company has strongly denied there has ever been a shortage of storage space or that families have been turned away.

Assistant Minister for Health Penioni Ravunawa confirmed that the Suva morgue is operated by Suva Funeral Directors under an agreement with the Ministry of Health.

The concerns come after the late Permanent Secretary for Health and Medical Services, Dr Jemesa Tudravu, highlighted the issue last year, saying overcrowded morgues were not only a challenge in the Western Division but were also affecting Suva.

Dr Tudravu said the problem was often caused by a spike in deaths, delays by families in organising burials and technical issues affecting morgue facilities.

Suva Funeral Directors owner Deevan Prasad has rejected the claims and said that the Assistant Minister's comments are incorrect.

Prasad says the facility can accommodate up to 78 bodies and normally has about 30 bodies at any given time, meaning there is always sufficient space available.

He says the Suva morgue also caters for Oceania Hospital and has never experienced overcrowding since it began operating in 2012.

According to Prasad, the only time the morgue exceeded its capacity was during the COVID-19 pandemic, when refrigerated containers were brought in to manage the increased number of deaths.

He says families have never been told to take the bodies of their loved ones elsewhere because there was no room at the facility.

Prasad also says delays by families in collecting bodies have never resulted in the morgue reaching capacity.

He says the Suva morgue is the largest in Fiji, serving communities from Navua through Suva to Nausori.

Prasad adds that he was shocked to hear the claims and believes they are false, adding that no family has ever been turned away due to a lack of storage space and that suggestions otherwise unfairly damage his company's reputation.

item.content:encoded:
As part of the annual commemoration, the village observed Delailasakau Day, paying tribute to the victims and remembering the tragic events of that day.

Fiji's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, His Excellency Ambassador Filipo Tarakinikini, led the wreath-laying ceremony in honour of those who lost their lives, while Inspector of Police Paulino Wakanini represented the Fiji Police Force at the solemn occasion.

The commemoration concluded with a soli to raise funds for the construction of the new St Francis of Assisi Church in Delailasakau Village.

item.title: Peer outreach worker urges Tavua families to get tested as HIV crisis deepens
item.description: Peer Outreach Worker Viliame Vauvau, also known as Willy Gold, will continue his HIV awareness and community outreach programme in the Tavua and Vatukoula corridors tomorrow and Tuesday. Vauvau says Fiji is facing a national HIV crisis and people should not ignore the growing number of cases.
item.content:encoded:
Peer Outreach Worker Viliame Vauvau, also known as Willy Gold, will continue his HIV awareness and community outreach programme in the Tavua and Vatukoula corridors tomorrow and Tuesday.

Vauvau says Fiji is facing a national HIV crisis and people should not ignore the growing number of cases.

Vauvau says his goal is to reduce stigma surrounding HIV, improve public awareness, encourage early testing and support people in accessing the health services they need.

Insert: Vauvau on assistance MC 23rd July

Vauvau says people should make time to visit their nearest health facility and get tested, as early diagnosis allows people to access treatment and support services.

He says every second person could be at risk because of factors such as drug abuse and unsafe sexual practices, and is urging everyone to take responsibility for their health.

He says the crisis is happening in Tavua as well, which is why he continues to educate people about HIV prevention, testing and treatment.

Vauvau says as part of his outreach work, he distributes male and female condoms, encourages people to know their HIV status through testing, and accompanies those who are hesitant or uncomfortable to attend HIV testing services on their own.

He also organises community talanoa sessions and works with the Ministry of Health and Medical Services to conduct community and home-based HIV testing.

He believes building trust through community engagement is key to improving health outcomes and creating a more informed and supportive community.

He will be in Tavua Town tomorrow around 6pm.

item.title: Fijians in Taupo provide meals to 70 people through M?ori Women's Refuge
item.description: The Taupo Satsang Ramayan Mandali, made up of Fijians, provided meals to residents at the Māori Women's Refuge in Taupo, New Zealand. Speaking to fijivillage News, Mandali President Dev Achari said the group provided meals to about 70 people.
item.content:encoded:
The Taupo Satsang Ramayan Mandali, made up of Fijians, provided meals to residents at the Māori Women's Refuge in Taupo, New Zealand.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Mandali President Dev Achari said the group provided meals to about 70 people.

Achari says the organisation plans to expand the initiative to support between 100 and 200 people in the future.

He says members of the organisation came together to prepare meals for people supported by the refuge, believing that everyone deserves a good meal regardless of their age, race or religion.

He says the meal donation is only the beginning of the organisation's community work this year.

Achari adds that the organisation hopes to work closely with the Māori Women's Refuge on future initiatives and continue assisting those in need.

item.title: Tolu Young becomes first Fijian to qualify for Commonwealth Games men's 50m freestyle final
item.description: Fiji has reached another historic milestone in international swimming after David Young, also known as Tolu Young, became the first Fijian to qualify for a Commonwealth Games men's 50 metres freestyle final. This is after clocking a blistering personal best time of 22.09 seconds in the semi finals in Glasgow, Scotland.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji has reached another historic milestone in international swimming after David Young, also known as Tolu Young, became the first Fijian to qualify for a Commonwealth Games men's 50 metres freestyle final.

This is after clocking a blistering personal best time of 22.09 seconds in the semi finals in Glasgow, Scotland.

Young produced the swim of his career to secure his place in the final, marking a breakthrough moment for Fiji Aquatics and Team Fiji on the international stage.

His performance has been widely celebrated, with Fiji Aquatics describing it as a phenomenal achievement that has made the entire nation proud.

His time of 22.09 seconds is one of Fiji's greatest achievements in international swimming and puts Young in contention for a Commonwealth Games medal.

Young will return to the pool for the men's 50 metres freestyle final, which will be held at 8am tomorrow , as Fiji eagerly awaits another historic performance.

item.title: AIIB approves US$80M in financing to improve Fiji's climate and disaster preparedness
item.description: In a statement the Bank says the funding is being provided under their Energy, Food Security and Economic Resilience Facility and is co-financed with the World Bank. They say together, the two institutions will provide US$230 million which is about FJ$516 million in fast-disbursing budget support to help implement the Government's reform programme.
item.content:encoded:
In a statement the Bank says the funding is being provided under their Energy, Food Security and Economic Resilience Facility and is co-financed with the World Bank.

They say together, the two institutions will provide US$230 million which is about FJ$516 million in fast-disbursing budget support to help implement the Government's reform programme.

The programme aims to strengthen Fiji's ability to respond to external economic shocks and climate-related disasters while improving the business environment.

It is expected by 2028 to expand disaster risk reduction coverage, improve public financial management for disaster preparedness, increase access to regulated financial services for small and medium-sized businesses, streamline regulations for low-risk tourism operators, expand digital payments, and improve nutrition and physical activity outcomes for children.

AIIB Chief Investment Officer Kim-See Lim says the financing provides timely support for Fiji's reform agenda while strengthening systems needed for long-term economic resilience.

Minister for Finance, Commerce and Business Development Esrom Immanuel welcomed the financing, saying it comes at an important time as Fiji advances key reforms to strengthen the economy and build resilience against future shocks.

He says the support complements the Government's commitment to prudent fiscal management, climate resilience, and creating a more enabling environment for businesses and investment.

The programme aligns with Fiji's National Development Plan 2025-2029 and Vision 2050 and further strengthens AIIB's partnership with Fiji.
